summary: The root ذلل primarily signifies being low, humble, or submissive, often in a gentle or easy manner. It can describe something made easy to use, like a path, or a person made subservient.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: َلَّ, aor. يَ ِلُّ, (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. ُلٌّ and ِلَّةٌ and مَ َلَّةٌ, (S, * M, MA, K,) or these three are simple substs., and the inf. n. is َلٌّ, (Msb,) and َلَالَةٌ (M, K) and ُلَالَةٌ, (K,) [ contr. of عَزَّ; (see ُلٌّ below;) i. e.] He, or it, was or became, low, base, vile, abject, mean, paltry, contemptible, despicable, ignominious, inglorious, abased, humble, and weak; (MA, Msb, K;) syn. هَانَ, (Msb, K,) and ضَعُفَ. (Msb.) َلَّ, (M, K,) and َلَّتْ, (M, Msb,) aor. as above, (M, K,) inf.

لّل, (M, Msb,) inf. n. تَ ْلِيلٌ, (Msb,) He made, or rendered, (M, Msb,) a man, (M,) and a beast, such as a horse and the like, (M, Msb,) easy, tractable, submissive, or manageable: (M, Msb:) [said of the former, it may be rendered he brought under, or into, subjection; or he subdued: and said of the latter, he broke, or trained: and said of any animal, he tamed.

ا لّهُ, (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. إِ ْلَالٌ, (TA,) He (God, Msb) lowered, abased, or humbled, him; or rendered him low, base, vile, abject, mean, paltry, contemptible, despicable, ignominious, inglorious, abased, humbled, and weak; (M, * Msb K, TA;) as also and: (K, TA:) all these signify the same. (S.) See also 10 ا لّ [as an intrans. verb] He (a man, S, M) became one whose companions were low, base, vile, &c. (S, M, K.) He became in a state, or condition, that was low, base, vile, &c. (S in art.

است لّهُ He saw him to be َلِيل [i. e. low, base, vile, &c.]: (M, K:) or he found him to be so; (TA;) as also. (K.) See also 4. است لّ البَعِيرَ الصَّعْبَ He plucked off the ticks from the refractory camel in order that he might experience pleasure [or relief ], and so become at ease, or tranquil, (M, K,) with him. (K.)
[ ا ْلَوْلَى, a verb of which one of the significations is mentioned in this art. in the K, belongs to art. لى.]
R. Q. 2 تَ َلْ َلَ [app. from ُلْ ُلٌ ] It was, or became, in a state of commotion, or agitation, and lax, slack, or pendulous. (K.)

ُلٌّ and and [all mentioned in the M and MA and K as inf. ns.] contr. of عِزٌّ; (S, M;) [i. e.] Lowness, baseness, vileness, abjectness, meanness, paltriness, contemptibleness, despicableness, ignominiousness, ingloriousness, abasement, humiliation, and weakness. (Msb, K. *) وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلِىٌّ مِنَ ال ُّلِّ, in the Kur [xvii.

ِلٌّ Easiness, tractableness, submissiveness, or manageableness; (S, M, K, and Ham p. 50; [mentioned in the M and Msb and K as an inf. n.;]) as also. (M, K, and Ham ubi suprà.) Hence the saying, بَعْضُ ال ِّلِّ أَبْقَى لِلْأَهْلِ وَالمَالِ [ Somewhat of submissiveness is most preservative of the family and the property ]: (S:) or أَبْقَى لِلْأَهْلِ وَالمَالِ, occurring in a trad.

ِلَّةٌ: see ُلٌّ. In the following verse, لِيَهْنِئْ تُرَاثِى لِٱمْرِئٍ غَيْرِ ِلَّةٍ صَنَابِرُ أُحْدَانٌ لِهُنَّ حَفِيفُ [ May my heritage give joy to a man not low, or base; slender arrows, singular of their kind, that have a whizzing sound ], the meaning is, غَيْرِ َلِيلٍ, or غَيْرِ ِى ِلَّةٍ; and صنابر is put in the nom. case as a substitute for تراث. (M.)

َلُولٌ Easy, tractable, submissive, or manageable; (S, M, Msb, K;) applied to a beast, such as a horse and the like, ( دَابَّة ), (S, M, Msb,) and to a man [&c.]; (M;) and so, applied to a man: (TA, as from the M: [but not found by me in the latter; and I believe that the right reading is َلَوْلًى, belonging to art. لى, q. v.:]) the former alike masc. and fem.: (M, TA:) pl. ُلُلٌ (S, M, Msb, K) and أَ ِلَّةٌ.

َلِيلٌ Low, base, vile, abject, mean, paltry, contemptible, despicable, ignominious, inglorious, lowered, brought low, abased, humbled, and weak; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) applied to a man; (T, S;) and signifies the same, as a sing.; (Ibn- 'Abbád, K:) or this latter is a pl. of the former, (T,) as also أَ ِلَّآءُ (S, M, Msb, K) and أَ ِلَّةٌ (T, S, Msb, K) and ِلَالٌ. (M, K.) [Also Gentle; and merciful. Hence,] أَ ِلَّةٍ عَلَى المُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الكَافِرينَ, in the Kur [v.
َلُولِىٌّ Good and easy in respect of natural disposition: pl. َلُولِيُّونَ. (Ibn-' Abbád, K. [In the CK, الخَلْقِ is erroneously put for الخُلُقِ.]) See also َلُولٌ.

ُلْ ُلٌ is sing. of َلَا ِلُ, which signifies The lower, or lowest, parts, (AZ, T, S,) that are next the ground, of a shirt, (S,) or of a long shirt; (AZ, T;) and IAar says that the sing. is, and, also; and they are also called َنَا ِنُ, pl. of ِنْ ِنٌ; (T;) and دَنَادِنُ: (K in art. دن:) or ُلْ ُلٌ and and and and all signify the lower, or lowest, parts of a long shirt (M, K) when it dangles and becomes old and worn out; (M;) as also َلَا ِلُ; (K;) [or rather] this last is pl.
ِلْ ِلٌ and ُلَ ِلٌ and َلَ ِلٌ and see ُلْ ُلٌ, in eight places.
ِلْ ِلَةٌ and ُلَ ِلَةٌ and َلَ ِلَةٌ and see ُلْ ُلٌ, in eight places.
ُلْ ُلَانُ النَّاسِ and ُلَيْ ِلَانُهُمْ: see ُلْ ُلٌ.
أَ َلٌّ [ More, and most, low, base, vile, &c.]: see أَخْنَعُ.
أَ ْلَالٌ as a pl. without a sing.: see ِلٌّ (of which it is also a pl.), in two places: and see ُلْ ُلٌ, last sentence.
مَ َلَّةٌ: see ُلٌّ. [Hence,] غَيْرُالمَ َلَّةِ (assumed tropical:) The wooden pin, peg, or stake: (S, K:) because its head is broken [or battered by beating]. (S.) [See عَيْرٌ.]

مُ َلَّلٌ: see َلِيلٌ. Also, [applied to palmtrees ( نَخْل ),] (assumed tropical:) Having the fruit thereof bent [ down ] in order that it may be [ easily ] gathered: [see also its verb (2):] so in the following verse of Imra-el-Keys: (Sgh, TA:) وَكَشْحٍ لَطِيفٍ كَالجَدِيلِ مُخَصَّرٍ وَسَاقٍ كَأُنْبُوبِ السَّقِىِّ المُ َلَّلِ meaning And a waist slender like the camel's nose-rein of [ twisted ] leather, thin; and a shank resembling, in the clearness of its colour, the stalk (lit.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
